Job Description Summary

As an intern of the product management team, you will be an active contributor to the innovation and competitiveness of control system solutions for power plants around the world.

The Controls Product Management Intern will support the Product Management team in the end-to-end development and lifecycle management of our control system products.

Job Description

Innovation
Are you passionate about innovation? Are you excited at the opportunity to electrify and decarbonize the world?

We operate with a founder’s mindset. We deliver innovation with passion, speed, and courage. We continuously challenge our thinking and are empowered to dream big and take smart risks.

Role Overview:

The intern will work closely with cross-functional teams, including engineering, supply chain, and marketing, to help define product vision, prioritize and track development, and ensure we are delivering maximum value to our customers.

Key Responsibilities

- Conduct customer, market, and stakeholder discovery; synthesize qualitative and quantitative inputs to identify and prioritize unmet needs.
- Assess current product and service capabilities against customer and business needs, identify meaningful gaps, and recommend prioritized roadmap options.
- Translate validated needs into clear, testable product requirements, acceptance criteria, and supporting documentation for Product Requirements Documents (PRDs).
- Develop evidence-based business cases that define the opportunity, customer value, assumptions, risks, costs, and expected outcomes.
- Research relevant industry and regulatory considerations and create lightweight prototypes, process flows, or visual concepts to help stakeholders evaluate proposed solutions, with guidance from technical and compliance experts.

May or June 2027 to August 2027 (Summer).

- Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Business, Finance, Engineering, Supply Chain Management, or a related field

- The required work location is Greenville, SC or Longmont, CO - 100% onsite.
- Must have the ability to work in the United States for an unlimited amount of time without sponsorship

- Minimum of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale or a 4.0 on a 5.0 scale cumulative GPA (without rounding)
- Knowledge of controls or industrial automation products.
- Prior internship or coursework experience in controls engineering, cost analysis, product management, or financial modeling.
- Familiarity with ERP systems (e.g., SAP) and data analysis software.
- Strong analytical skills and proficiency in Microsoft Excel; experience with data visualization tools is a plus.
- Excellent attention to detail and ability to work with large data sets.
- Effective written and verbal communication skills.

Job Description

Summer Internship Program
Our paid Summer Internship Program is designed to provide students with an immersive, hands-on experience within the aerospace and defense industry. Interns work alongside AV team members on meaningful projects involving cutting-edge technology while developing professional relationships, strategic problem-solving skills, and practical experience in a full-time work environment.

This is a 12-week, onsite program intended for highly motivated and passionate students who are currently enrolled in college or are recent graduates. Applicants must have a minimum 3.0 GPA, with a preference for students at the junior level or above.

Our program has been recognized by Yello and WayUp as one of the Top 100 Internship Programs in the United States for multiple years.

Depending on the team and location, students who are willing to relocate for their internship may be eligible for a relocation and housing reimbursement stipend.

AV offers internship opportunities across various teams and locations throughout the United States. Specific team, location, and program details will be discussed during the interview process.

Summary

As an Embedded Software Engineering Intern, you will work alongside experienced engineers to design, develop, and test embedded software for unmanned aerial and robotic systems. You’ll gain hands-on experience in real-world development, writing software that runs on microcontrollers, processors, and other hardware used in flight systems, sensors, and payloads.

You’ll contribute to projects at various stages of the development lifecycle — from prototyping and integration to testing and validation — while learning industry best practices in embedded software development.

Position Responsibilities

- Assist in writing and testing embedded software for systems such as autopilots, sensors, radios, and other onboard components.

- Help implement software in C/C++ for real-time and bare-metal systems using microcontrollers and embedded platforms.

- Support the integration of embedded software with hardware, including debugging with lab tools (oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, etc.).

- Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including electrical, systems, and mechanical engineers, to ensure cohesive development.

- Participate in peer reviews, software documentation, and configuration management processes.

- Contribute to lab testing and field testing of embedded systems in support of real-world mission scenarios.

- Assist in the development of prototypes and proof-of-concept demonstrations.

Basic Qualifications (Required Skills & Experience)

- Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field.

- Basic knowledge of embedded systems and microcontrollers.

- Familiarity with programming languages such as C, C++, or Python.

- Understanding of low-level software concepts, such as memory management, interrupts, or device drivers.

- Exposure to hardware communication protocols like I2C, SPI, UART, or CAN.

- Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills.

- Effective verbal and written communication.

- Ability to work collaboratively in a team environment.

Preferred Qualifications & Competencies

- Hands-on experience with microcontroller platforms (e.g., STM32, Arduino, Raspberry Pi, or similar).

- Familiarity with RTOS environments (e.g., FreeRTOS, Zephyr).

- Exposure to Linux-based development or embedded Linux environments.

- Experience with lab equipment (e.g., oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, multimeters).

- Interest in aerospace, robotics, or autonomous systems.

- Initiative, curiosity, and a passion for learning and innovation.

Physical Demands

- Ability to work in an office and R&D environment (Constant)

- Required to sit, type, and use office/lab equipment for extended periods (Frequent)

- Occasional hands-on work in lab and field test environments may be required

Clearance Level

No Clearance

Robotics Engineering Intern
San Francisco · Onsite · Internship

About Bracket Bot

We believe planet earth can thrive and be alive. Robots should manufacture goods, clean roadways, tidy our rooms, build more homes, cook healthy food, and lower the cost of living. We aren’t quite there yet, robots are too expensive, too difficult to program, fragile, and unfriendly. Bracket Bot is changing that.

We believe that robots are currently in the ENIAC era and we are bringing them to the Macbook era. We believe in high performance engineering teams where everyone you work with is what you imagined Bell Labs employees to be like. Intelligent, scrappy, dedicated, kind.

At Bracket Bot, we have a few objectives. We are working to make the ideal role model of a company, one where everyone is at the top of their field, inventing new ways to solve the problems we face across mechanical, electrical, software, and machine learning. What does a company that creates entirely new ways that teams work together look like? A company that invents new materials for lighter weight actuators and structures? A company that creates and publishes new inverse kinematics algorithms for robots? A company that is thinking radically differently, and executing on another level.

In every field there are small teams who did something their peers had decided was impossible. The 10-second barrier in sprinting, or the eight engineers who left Motorola and made the 6502 for 10x lower cost than other chips at the time making the personal computer possible. SpaceX has landed the same rocket 36 times. Bracket Bot believes actuated, alive machines can be glorious, affordable, easy to use, and ubiquitous, and we are pulling that future forward.

Our products are a mirror of what we think about the world, on engineering & research, and what we think should be introduced into the world. In history, there are simply products that should exist, and only once created, are obvious in hindsight. Bracket Bot’s mission is to introduce as many of these products into the world as possible. We believe there are hundreds of these in the space of robotics. Across physical robot hardware, software and operating system; the infrastructure and distributed systems they connect to; the AI inference they run, both local and cloud, and so much more.

Our first product, Bracket Bot 1, exemplifies what a small team of highly talented people can do. At Bracket Bot, we genuinely believe 100x engineers exist, and a room full of them can create things that dozens of other companies have failed to do. We’ve brought to market a robot that is 10x lower cost than any other robot in its category, while out performing them on manipulation, autonomous navigation, speech interaction, and developer UX.

We’re backed by Fifty Years (Scott Phoenix), BoxGroup, SV Angel, Betaworks, Pace Capital, angels including Nat Friedman, Logan Kilpatrick (Google AI), Guillermo Rauch (Vercel) and others from Tesla AI, Physical Intelligence, and Markforged.

About the role

Robotics brings mechanical systems, electronics, software, and machine learning together. The fastest way to learn is to build, test, and debug the whole system.

We’re hiring a Robotics Engineering Intern to contribute to hands-on engineering projects with the Bracket Bot team. You’ll help build and improve robots, investigate failures, and take scoped projects from an idea to a tested result.

Your work will draw on your strengths while giving you exposure to the other disciplines that make a robot work.

What you’ll do

- Build, integrate, and test robot hardware or software with the engineering team.

- Help reproduce failures, collect useful measurements, and debug system behavior.

- Develop prototypes, tools, or tests that support robot development.

- Document results and communicate what worked, what failed, and what to try next.

- Own a scoped engineering project through implementation and verification.

What we’re looking for

- Hands-on engineering projects that show curiosity and follow-through.

- A foundation in mechanical, electrical, software, or robotics engineering.

- Willingness to build, measure, debug, and learn unfamiliar systems.

- Clear communication and the ability to ask useful questions.

- Care for the quality of your work and enthusiasm for physical robots.

Nice to have

- Personal, university, lab, or competition robotics projects.

- Experience with CAD, electronics, programming, or practical fabrication.

- Experience building test tools or documenting technical projects.

Important notes

- This is a hands-on internship based onsite in San Francisco.

- We value evidence of things you’ve built and problems you’ve worked through.

- You’ll collaborate closely with engineers on real robot development.

Bracket Bot is an equal opportunity employer. We’re building a diverse team and welcome applicants from all backgrounds.
